rv.q: Lewis seems less interested in wowing us with his skills of illusion and uncanny perception than in getting us to laugh — and he does, big time. That's the real magic.
Like its sister shows, this is a goofy, but intelligent mix of silliness and sophistication.
This troupe is always a pleasure to spend an evening with.

Even so, Mind Mangler provides a fair amount of entertainment; and if you bring the kids, so much the better as it provides them with adult (as opposed to juvenile) entertainment they can howl at and feel quite sophisticated.
The two-hour show, directed by Hannah Sharkey, is too long for its good.
But if you've seen the other "...Goes Wrong" productions, there is little sense of surprise, and, before long, a feeling of sameness sets in; you can set the setups from a mile away.
Unexplainably, Lewis does indulge in several successful feats of magic that seem at odds with his character’s bad luck.
There is no reason to dissuade anyone from going to the theatre for a night out, simply to have a few laughs and a good time.
Mind Mangler: A Night of Tragic Illusion, Mischief’s newest play—which opened tonight at New World Stages—is true to Mischief form: goofy, haphazard, and very entertaining.

The Mind Mangler is a half-good magician, and the show revolves around this conceit; its magic charms the audience with sleight of hand, and as a parody of a mediocre magician, it entertains with colorful turns of phrase, an endless slew of one-liners, and of course his actively incompetent tricks.
Although some of the illusions actually worked, they are overshadowed by the planned screw-ups.

cn.t: Mischief Theatre's latest delivers silly, clever comedy with strong audience interaction, though critics find it a lesser entry in the "Goes Wrong" franchise.
